rationales.1: The twelve-month band above each entry makes season fit readable at a glance and the entries are grouped by sowing window, but price and stock sit in small type at the end of a long text block rather than in a scannable column.
rationales.2: Price, stock language and the single add-to-basket path are conventional on the product page, though the catalog offers no per-item buy affordance and only one entry carries a visible link to its packet page.
rationales.3: Out of stock, the low-count warning, the estimated germination flag, the withheld price rendered as 'Price pending — ask us', and UK-only shipping stated in the header are all honest and visible before intent forms.
rationales.4: Type is legible and nothing depends on hover, but the catalog leans on small metadata text and thin month cells that are demanding for older readers at default zoom.
rationales.5: One restrained palette, a consistent rule-and-margin rhythm, and the same month band on both surfaces read as a single system, with the margin notes aligned to a real column.
rationales.6: Sowing window, plant-out, flowering, difficulty, germination, grower notes and companions are all present in a clear order, so a first-time gardener can decide without leaving the page.
rationales.7: The almanac framing — the year as a band, the shop's own marginalia — is a genuine two-person shop idea carried through content, layout and voice rather than borrowed gloss.
rationales.8: The novelty sits in the almanac metaphor and the marginal notes while the money path stays plain, though the catalog's near-absent buy affordance pushes the break closer to mechanics than is comfortable.
rationales.9: Lines like 'shelved under the window it wants' and the margin notes sound like a specific grower talking, unhurried and particular.
rationales.10: Season-first grouping and the anchor links to each window serve a repeat visitor checking what is sowable now, and both surfaces share the same almanac vocabulary.

rationales.1: Cards on labelled shelves put price and stock state on a consistent baseline in every tile, so season fit and availability are all readable in one pass.
rationales.2: Price sits bottom-left and stock bottom-right in every card, the shipping constraint is a persistent chip, and the product page keeps quantity plus a single primary button in conventional order.
rationales.3: Out of stock is called out in a distinct colour, the low-count line is explicit, the estimated germination is flagged, the null price reads 'Price on request', and UK-only shipping is visible on both surfaces.
rationales.4: Large card targets, generous line height and a full-width mobile stack suit older readers on tablets, with no information hidden behind hover.
rationales.5: The shelf-and-packet motif, dotted card divider, and one warm palette hold across both surfaces with even spacing and aligned tiles.
rationales.6: The buy box sits directly under the summary and is followed by the year table, grower notes and companions, so the decision is complete above the fold on desktop.
rationales.7: The seed rack by the shop door is a true small-shop idea and the packet illustrations carry it into the visual layer without boutique gloss.
rationales.8: Breaks are limited to the packet-card art direction and shelf naming while price, stock and basket mechanics stay entirely conventional.
rationales.9: Warm and specific in places like 'Two of us keep it stocked' and 'From our potting shed', though the item copy is more catalogue-plain than the framing promises.
rationales.10: Shelf headers plus the month filter let a returning shopper see what is sowable now immediately, and the rack vocabulary ties the two surfaces together.

rationales.1: Price and stock are consistently placed per entry, but the flat numbered list has no season grouping, so working out what is sowable now means reading every row's sowing line.
rationales.2: The money path is plain and conventional on the product page, though only the first catalog entry exposes a link to its packet and the rest offer no route forward.
rationales.3: Out of stock, the low-count line, the estimated germination flag, the pending price and UK-only shipping are all stated plainly, though the shipping note is set in the smallest type on the page.
rationales.4: Body copy and the buy controls are comfortably sized with no hover dependence, but the metadata rows and shipping line drop to a small size that taxes older eyes.
rationales.5: A disciplined single-column list with consistent rules and one palette, though the very narrow measure against wide empty margins leaves the desktop catalog looking underfilled.
rationales.6: Price, stock, sowing table, grower notes and companions are all present in a sensible order, with the buy box placed early enough to decide from.
rationales.7: The numbered seed list is a coherent quiet idea but reads as a generic catalogue convention rather than something only this two-person shop could claim.
rationales.8: Novelty is confined to the numbering and the restrained typographic treatment, leaving the checkout-adjacent mechanics untouched.
rationales.9: 'Read slowly, choose well' has some character, but the entry copy is functional description that a competitor could publish largely unchanged.
rationales.10: The arbitrary numbered order and absence of any season grouping mean a repeat visitor checking what is newly sowable must scan the whole list.
